summary: Franz Aubrey Metcalf is a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies who earned his Ph.D. at the University of Chicago. He served as an instructor at California State University, Los Angeles (attested 2002–2006).

Franz Bernhard (1931–1971) worked in Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Ernst Waldschmidt (~1951–1957) and completed his habilitation at Goethe University Frankfurt (~1963–1965). In 1966, he was appointed Professor and Director at the University of Hamburg.

Franz Bopp (1791–1867) was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Karl Joseph Hieronymus Windischmann, Antoine-Isaac Silvestre de Sacy, and Antoine-Léonard de Chézy, and at London and Göttingen. He served as Chair of Sanskrit at Humboldt University of Berlin (1821–1867).

Franz Heinrich Trithen (1820–1854) was a linguist and Indologist who studied under Franz Bopp at Frederick William University and Humboldt University of Berlin. He worked at the British Museum (~1844–1848) and as Professor of Modern Languages at Oxford (~1848–1854).

Franz Kielhorn (1840–1908) was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Adolf Friedrich Stenzler and Albrecht Weber. He was Professor of Oriental Languages at Deccan College (1866) and Professor of Sanskrit at the University of Göttingen (~1881–1908).
Franz Xaver Erhard is a Tibetologist who earned master's degrees from the Free University of Berlin and Humboldt University of Berlin, and completed a Ph.D. at the University of Bonn (attested 2003).

Franz-Karl Ehrhard is a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Lambert Schmithausen and habilitated at Hamburg. He directed the Nepal-German Manuscript Preservation Project (1988–1993) and held an endowed seat and professorship at Munich (2001, 2006–2012).
François Gros (1933–2021) was an Indologist who studied at the University of Lyon (~1951–1956). He later served on the faculty at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1977–2002).
François Jacob (1920–2013) studied at Lycée Carnot and the Paris Medical Faculty (~1938–1947). He held a post at the Collège de France from 1964 to 1991.

Françoise Pommaret is a Tibetologist and historian who studied at INALCO (~1975–1979) and the University of Paris (~1985–1997). She served as a lecturer at INALCO and became Directeur de recherche at the CNRS in 2002.
Françoise Robin is a Tibetologist who studied under Heather Stoddard from ~1996 to 2003. She took up a post at the Institut national des langues et civilisations orientales in ~2005.
Fred Pfeil (1949–2005) worked in Buddhist studies and other fields. He studied at Amherst College (~1967–1971) and held a post at Oregon State University.
Frederick M. Asher (1941–2021) was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He spent his career at the University of Minnesota, serving as Professor from ~1970 to 2021.

Frederick William Thomas (1867–1956) was an Indologist and Tibetologist educated at Trinity College, Cambridge. He served as Librarian at the India Office Library (~1903–1927) and Boden Professor of Sanskrit at Oxford (1927–1937).

Frederik David Kan Bosch (1887–1967) was an Indologist and archaeologist who headed the Archaeological Service in the Netherlands East Indies (~1916–1936). He later held posts at Utrecht University (1938–1945) and Leiden University (1946–1957).

Fredrik Barth (1928–2016) studied at Chicago and Cambridge under Edmund Leach. He held posts at the universities of Bergen (~1961–1972) and Oslo (~1974–1985), as well as Harvard (~1989–1996), Emory (~1989–2008), and Boston University (~1997–2008).
Friederike Assandri works in Sinology and religious studies. She studied under Gunther-Dietz Sontheimer as a Ph.D. student at Heidelberg University, where she also held a post (attested 2013).

Friedhelm Hardy (1943–2004) was a scholar of Indology and religious studies. He served on the faculty at King's College London (~1974–2004) and as Wilde Lecturer in Comparative Religion at the University of Oxford (1985–1987).

Friedrich Alexander Bischoff (1928–2009) worked in Sinology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. He earned his Ph.D. from the University of Paris (~1954–1959) and served as Professor of Sinology at the University of Hamburg (~1976–1982).

Friedrich August Rosen (1805–1837) was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Franz Bopp (~1824–1826). He held posts as Professor of Oriental Languages at University College London (~1828–1836) and Professor of Sanskrit at the University of London (1834).
